units.requirement_text: Commissioned generation, by each group of generating units at a single plant location, with an aggregate highest rated net Real Power capability of the preceding 12 calendar months equal to or exceeding 1500 MW in a single Interconnection. For each group of generating units, the only BES Cyber Systems that meet this criterion are those shared BES Cyber Systems that could, within 15 minutes, adversely impact the reliable operation of any combination of units that in aggregate equal or exceed 1500 MW in a single Interconnection.
units.section_text:
3.4 Categorize and Apply the Impact Rating Criteria 
3.4.1 
Transmission Planning  in consultation with Transmission System Operations will: 
3.4.1.1 
Step 4: Categorize the identified BES Facilities utilizing the output from the previous step 
to those entries that qualify as BES Facilities in sequential steps, using Attachment 1 of 
the CIP-002-5.1a standard document. 
• 
Medium (Generation and Transmission facilities criteria 2.1 – 2.10) 
• 
High (Control Centers criteria 1.1 – 1.4) 
• 
Medium (selected Control Centers criteria 2.11 – 2.13) 
• 
Low (Remaining BES Facilities) 
Note: The ordering above is deliberate because of the dependencies between High, Medium, and Low. 
3.4.2 OT Security & Compliance will: 
3.4.2.1 
For each BES Asset identified in Step 4 above, Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) will 
establish an inventory of the candidate Cyber Assets associated with High and Medium 
Impact BES Assets and determine whether each Cyber Asset meets the CIP definition of 
“BES Cyber Asset.” This determination is made by considering whether the loss, 
degradation, misoperation, or compromise of the Cyber Asset would have an Adverse 
Impact on the BES within 15 minutes. This will establish a BES Cyber Asset inventory list 
for each BES Asset.  
Note: Refer to key tips in ERO Enterprise-Endorsed Implementation Guidance: CIP-002-5.1 R1 
Identify and Categorize BES Cyber Systems and Cyber Assets (MRO SC) for additional guidance 
when applying the BES Cyber Asset classification to Cyber Assets.  
 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 9 of 13 
 
3.4.2.2 
Since the identification of the Controls Centers draws from assets that are Medium 
Impact, the Medium Impact rating assessment of Cyber Assets should be performed 
before the High Impact rating assessment. 
3.4.2.3 
Using the BES Cyber Asset definition, develop and document a list of BCAs and if 
appropriate, group by BES Cyber System. See section 3.5. 
3.4.2.4 Determine the associated Electronic Access Control and Monitoring Systems (EACMS), 
Physical Access Control Systems (PACS), and Protected Cyber Assets (PCA) with each 
BES Cyber System. 
3.4.2.5 The classification exercise is performed by completing the Asset Inventory Classification 
Template. The Asset Inventory Classification Template process will assist in the 
Classification of the Cyber Asset. 
3.4.2.6 Document the list within OTAM1 and include the following information.  
• 
Cyber Asset Name 
• 
Classification (BES Cyber Asset, EACMS, PACS, PCA) 
• 
Impact Rating 
• 
BES Cyber System ID 
• 
Asset ID 
• 
IP Address 
• 
Function 
• 
Manufacturer 
• 
Model 
• 
Connectivity 
• 
Operating System 
3.4.3 For any Low Impact BES Asset identified, LSPG will determine whether the asset has any 
associated Cyber Assets that meet the definition of BES Cyber Assets.

1.1 
Purpose 
The purpose of this process is to enable the effective implementation of NERC Reliability Standard 
CIP-002-5.1a, which requires registered entities to identify and categorize BES Cyber Systems and 
their associated BES Cyber Assets for the application of cyber security requirements, commensurate 
with the Adverse Impact that loss, compromise, or misuse of those BES Cyber Systems could have on 
the reliable operation of the BES.

3.9 Testing of Backup Information  
3.9.1 
For High and Medium Impact BCS at control centers and their associated EACMS and PACS, 
OT, EMS, and Field Ops shall test a representative sample of information used to recover BCS 
functionality at least once every fifteen (15) calendar months to ensure that the information 
is useable and is compatible with current configurations.

units.section_text:
3.1.6 
Mitigate the Introduction of Malicious Code (Section 1.4) 
Prior to use on applicable systems, the OT Security Operations team utilizes Antivirus Software (AV) 
as the method to mitigate the introduction of malicious code in accordance with the OT Malicious 
Code Prevention Process. During the build process of a TCA, AV software is installed.  
TCA are required to be connected to the network on a defined date every month to receive security 
patch updates as described in Section 2.1.5 above. During the connection to the network, TCA will 
receive AV software and pattern file updates to the current version(s). TCA connected to the network 
since the most recent monthly update and before the next scheduled monthly update may receive 
additional AV updates. Prior to connecting to applicable systems, TCA must have updated AV 
signature files at a minimum of monthly during patching cycles. Documentation of monthly AV 
software and pattern file updates is tracked through the OT Change Management Procedure. 
In the event a TCA does not receive the monthly AV update, the TCA is pulled from service and 
required to be updated to the most current version(s) prior to connecting to any applicable systems.  
If a TCA is identified as having malicious code, OT Security Operations follows the OT Security 
Incident Response Plan.

units.section_text:
1.1 
Purpose 
LSPG has developed the Transient Cyber Asset (TCA) and Removable Media (RM) Plan to prevent 
unauthorized access or malware propagation to high impact and medium impact BES Cyber Systems 
and associated Protected Cyber Assets (PCAs). This plan is also applicable to low impact BES Cyber 
Systems for the use of TCA and RM. 
The processes defined in this plan are intended to act as a component in an overall program to ensure 
the proper implementation of cyber security controls around TCA and RM as well as to continually 
improve the overall security posture of LSPG’s cyber security program.
cited_sentences: This plan is also applicable to low impact BES Cyber Systems for the use of TCA and RM.

units.section_text:
3.3 Transient Cyber Asset (TCA) and Removable Media (RM) Usage 
3.3.1 
Any use of a TCA or RM must comply with Transient Cyber Asset and Removable Media 
Security Plan.  
3.3.2 The SME is responsible for assuring their change has all the required work tasks for TCAs.  
3.3.3 When using RM, the SME is responsible for scanning the RM in a TCA prior to plugging into an 
applicable Cyber Asset to ensure there is no malicious code.   
3.3.4 The SME documents in the notes section of the change record that RM was utilized for the 
change, the location where the RM was used, and with which Cyber Assets.  
3.3.5 The SME will upload a screenshot of the scan to the change record. The date and time of the 
scan must be visible in the screenshot.

units.section_text:
3.3.4 Mitigate the Introduction of Malicious Code (Section 3.2, 3.2.1) 
LSPG uses RM to perform maintenance on applicable systems. As a protective measure, OT Security 
Operations logically disables ports not in use. Prior to being plugged into a BES Cyber System or PCA, 
the user plugs the RM into a TCA which has current signature files per Section 2.1.6 and scans the RM 
for possible malicious code. If malicious code is found during the scan of the RM, the TCA should be 
quarantined and rescanned prior to being connected to the BCS or PCA. Evidence of using RM and the 
scan is maintained in the change management solution repository, per the OT Change Management 
Procedure. 
If the RM is identified as having malicious code prior to connecting to an applicable system, LSPG 
follows the OT Security Incident Response Plan.

units.requirement_text: Each Responsible Entity shall review and obtain CIP Senior Manager approval at least once every 15 calendar months for one or more documented cyber security policies that collectively address the following topics:
units.section_text:
3.1 
Designation of CIP Senior Manager 
To ensure our commitment to compliance with the NERC CIP Standards’ obligations, LS Power has 
assigned a single CIP Senior Manager with overall responsibility and authority for leading and managing 
the Company’s implementation and adherence to the NERC CIP Standards. 
The designated NERC CIP Senior Manager may delegate certain responsibilities as permitted by the 
NERC CIP Standards. In addition to setting forth the CIP Senior Manager Designation commitment, this 
Process provides the procedures to be followed for CIP Senior Manager related designation and 
delegation responsibilities to ensure continued compliance.  
3.1.1 
The NERC CIP Senior Manager is designated by LS Power’s Chief Operating Officer (COO) in 
coordination with business unit and other relevant senior leadership. The official designation of 
the CIP Senior Manager is documented in accordance with Appendix A of this process, LS 
Power NERC CIP Senior Manager Designation. 
3.1.2 
The CIP Senior Manager must approve LS Power Cyber Security Policies for high impact, 
medium impact and assets containing low BES Cyber Systems in accordance with CIP-003-8 
(CIP-003-9, effective 4/1/26) R1 at least once every 15 calendar months. This approval may not 
be delegated however the CIP Senior Manager may delegate other responsibilities as described 
within this policy. Refer to Section 3.2 below and CIP-003-8 (CIP-003-9, effective 4/1/26) 
Cyber Security Policies. 
3.1.3 
Any changes to the CIP Senior Manager shall be documented within 30 calendar days of the 
effective date of the change. (Refer to Appendix A for designation form).

If a CIP Exceptional Circumstance is declared, the requirement for CIP-004-7 R2.2 can be temporarily 
suspended.  The event that caused the CIP Exceptional Circumstance, its duration and affected 
individuals must be documented and archived according to the OT CIP Exceptional Circumstance

units.requirement_text: Declaring and responding to CIP Exceptional Circumstances.
units.section_text:
3.9 Declaring and responding to CIP Exceptional Circumstances 
Note: The processes for declaring a CIP Exceptional Circumstance covers high impact and 
medium impact BCS, and assets containing low impact BCS. 
3.9.1 
The CIP Senior Manager, or approved delegate, may declare an emergency as allowed per the 
CIP Exceptional Circumstance Procedure and may suspend any or all the following cyber 
security requirements: 
3.9.1.1 
Requirement to complete security training prior to authorization for unescorted physical 
access and/or authorization for electronic access to BES Cyber Systems (CIP-004 R2.2), 
3.9.1.2 
Requirement to authorize electronic or physical access based on need (CIP-004 R4.1), 
3.9.1.3 
Requirement for continuous visitor escort while within a Physical Security Perimeter (CIP-
006 R2.1), 
3.9.1.4 
Requirement for manual or automatic logging of visitor access to a Physical Security 
Perimeter (CIP-006 R2.2), 
3.9.1.5 
Requirement to retain applicable (security monitoring) event logs for at least the last 90 
consecutive calendar days (CIP-007 R4.3), and 
3.9.1.6 
Allow for Transient Cyber Assets and Removable Media that include the sections in 
Attachment 1 (CIP-010 R4, CIP-003 Att. 1 Sections 5.1 and 5.2). 
LSPG shall document the suspension of any of these cyber security policies including the reason and 
duration. Delegates are documented in a separate document maintained by the Reliability Compliance 
department.

units.section_text:
1.1 
Purpose 
This Policy establishes requirements for effective implementation of NERC Reliability Standards, 
including declaring and responding to a CIP Exceptional Circumstance. Detailed plans, implementation 
procedures and work instructions support this Policy. 
It is the policy of LSPG to comply with all applicable provisions of the NERC Reliability Standards.
cited_sentences: This Policy establishes requirements for effective implementation of NERC Reliability Standards, including declaring and responding to a CIP Exceptional Circumstance.

units.section_text:
3.2 Declaring CIP Exceptional Circumstances 
 
Figure 3-1 CIP Exceptional Circumstances Definition Analysis 
3.2.1 
CECs can be declared in anticipation of an event, during an event, or documented after an 
emergency event. Refer to Figure 3-1 for the circumstances that can cause a CEC. 
3.2.2 LSPG requires a CEC to be declared by the CIP Senior Manager or delegate (per NERC CIP 
Senior Manager Delegations procedure). 
3.2.3 The CIP Senior Manager or delegate will designate the Emergency Event Coordinator after 
the CEC is approved

units.section_text:
3.5.2 Cyber Security Incident Response Plan Implementation and Testing Process (R2) 
3.5.2.1 
For high impact and medium impact BCS, and their associated EACMS, LSPG shall document 
and implement a Cyber Security Incident response plan to collectively include each of the 
applicable requirement parts in CIP-008-6 Table R2 – Cyber Security Incident Response Plan 
Implementation and Testing: 
• 
Test each Cyber Security Incident response plan(s) at least once every 15 calendar 
months using one of the following scenarios: 
o 
By responding to an actual Reportable Cyber Security Incident, 
o 
With a paper drill or tabletop exercise of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident, or 
o 
With an operational exercise of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident (Part 2.1). 
• 
Use the Cyber Security Incident response plan(s) when responding to a Reportable 
Cyber Security Incident or performing an exercise of a Reportable Cyber Security 
Incident. LSPG shall document deviations from the plan(s) taken during the response 
to the incident or exercise (Part 2.2), and 
• 
Retain records related to Reportable Cyber Security Incidents (Part 2.3). 
3.5.2.2 
For assets containing low impact BCS, LSPG shall test the Cyber Security Incident response 
plan(s) at least once every 36 calendar months by: 
o 
Responding to an actual Reportable Cyber Security Incident,

units.section_text:
3.1 
Designation of CIP Senior Manager 
To ensure our commitment to compliance with the NERC CIP Standards’ obligations, LS Power has 
assigned a single CIP Senior Manager with overall responsibility and authority for leading and managing 
the Company’s implementation and adherence to the NERC CIP Standards. 
The designated NERC CIP Senior Manager may delegate certain responsibilities as permitted by the 
NERC CIP Standards. In addition to setting forth the CIP Senior Manager Designation commitment, this 
Process provides the procedures to be followed for CIP Senior Manager related designation and 
delegation responsibilities to ensure continued compliance.  
3.1.1 
The NERC CIP Senior Manager is designated by LS Power’s Chief Operating Officer (COO) in 
coordination with business unit and other relevant senior leadership. The official designation of 
the CIP Senior Manager is documented in accordance with Appendix A of this process, LS 
Power NERC CIP Senior Manager Designation. 
3.1.2 
The CIP Senior Manager must approve LS Power Cyber Security Policies for high impact, 
medium impact and assets containing low BES Cyber Systems in accordance with CIP-003-8 
(CIP-003-9, effective 4/1/26) R1 at least once every 15 calendar months. This approval may not 
be delegated however the CIP Senior Manager may delegate other responsibilities as described 
within this policy. Refer to Section 3.2 below and CIP-003-8 (CIP-003-9, effective 4/1/26) 
Cyber Security Policies. 
3.1.3 
Any changes to the CIP Senior Manager shall be documented within 30 calendar days of the 
effective date of the change. (Refer to Appendix A for designation form).

units.section_text:
7.3 Security Incident Response Plan Updates 
7.3.1 
No later than ninety (90) calendar days after the completion of a test or actual response to a 
Reportable Cyber Security Incident response:  
7.3.1.1 
Any lessons learned or the absence of any lessons learned shall be documented on the 
Security Incident Investigation Form. 
7.3.1.2 
This Plan shall be updated based on any documented lessons learned associated with 
the plan.  
7.3.1.3 
Each person or group with a defined role in this Plan shall be notified of the updates 
made as a result of testing the plan or an actual Reportable Cyber Security Incident. 
7.3.1.4 
Specific after-action items, not including procedure updates, should be identified and 
tracked in Compliance Tracking Tool to closure. 
7.3.2 No later than sixty (60) calendar days after a change to the roles or responsibilities or a 
change in technology that would impact the ability to execute this procedure:  
7.3.2.1 
This Plan shall be updated to reflect the change(s).  
7.3.2.2 
Notification shall be sent to each person or group with a defined role in Section 3.2 that 
the evidence is located in the LSPG Compliance Tracking tool. 
7.3.3 Records generated from a Reportable Cyber Security incident shall be maintained for a 
minimum of three (3) years, or longer if directed by the Reliability Compliance Team to retain 
longer due to an investigation.

Note: The processes for declaring a CIP Exceptional Circumstance covers high impact and

The CIP Senior Manager, or approved delegate, may declare an emergency as allowed per the 
CIP Exceptional Circumstance Procedure and may suspend any or all the following cyber 
security requirements:

Requirement to complete security training prior to authorization for unescorted physical 
access and/or authorization for electronic access to BES Cyber Systems (CIP-004 R2.2), 
3.9.1.2

3.9.1.3 
Requirement for continuous visitor escort while within a Physical Security Perimeter (CIP-
006 R2.1), 
3.9.1.4 
Requirement for manual or automatic logging of visitor access to a Physical Security 
Perimeter (CIP-006 R2.2), 
3.9.1.5 
Requirement to retain applicable (security monitoring) event logs for at least the last 90 
consecutive calendar days (CIP-007 R4.3), and 
3.9.1.6 
Allow for Transient Cyber Assets and Removable Media that include the sections in 
Attachment 1 (CIP-010 R4, CIP-003 Att. 1 Sections 5.1 and 5.2). 
LSPG shall document the suspension of any of these cyber security policies including the reason and 
duration. Delegates are documented in a separate document maintained by the Reliability Compliance 
department.

1.1 
Purpose 
LSPG has developed the Transient Cyber Asset (TCA) and Removable Media (RM) Plan to prevent 
unauthorized access or malware propagation to high impact and medium impact BES Cyber Systems 
and associated Protected Cyber Assets (PCAs). This plan is also applicable to low impact BES Cyber 
Systems for the use of TCA and RM. 
The processes defined in this plan are intended to act as a component in an overall program to ensure 
the proper implementation of cyber security controls around TCA and RM as well as to continually 
improve the overall security posture of LSPG’s cyber security program.

3.3 Transient Cyber Asset (TCA) and Removable Media (RM) Usage 
3.3.1 
Any use of a TCA or RM must comply with Transient Cyber Asset and Removable Media 
Security Plan.  
3.3.2 The SME is responsible for assuring their change has all the required work tasks for TCAs.  
3.3.3 When using RM, the SME is responsible for scanning the RM in a TCA prior to plugging into an 
applicable Cyber Asset to ensure there is no malicious code.   
3.3.4 The SME documents in the notes section of the change record that RM was utilized for the 
change, the location where the RM was used, and with which Cyber Assets.  
3.3.5 The SME will upload a screenshot of the scan to the change record. The date and time of the 
scan must be visible in the screenshot.

3.7.4 Transient Cyber Assets and Removable Media (R4) 
3.7.4.1 
For high impact and medium impact BCS, LSPG shall implement, except during CIP 
Exceptional Circumstances, one or more documented plan(s) for Transient Cyber Assets and 
Removable Media: 
• 
Transient Cyber Assets 
o 
Transient Cyber Asset Management

o 
Transient Cyber Asset Authorization 
o 
Software Vulnerability Mitigation 
o 
Introduction of Malicious Code Mitigation 
o 
Unauthorized Use Mitigation  
• 
Removable Media 
o 
Removable Media Authorization 
o 
Malicious Code Mitigation 
3.7.4.2 
For assets containing low impact BCS, LSPG shall implement, except during CIP Exceptional 
Circumstances, one or more documented plan(s) to mitigate the risk of the introduction of 
malicious code to low impact BCS through the use of Transient Cyber Assets (TCA) and 
Removable Media (RM). The plan(s) shall include: 
• 
For Transient Cyber Assets managed by LSPG – use one or a combination of the 
following in an ongoing or on-demand manner per TCA capability (Att. 1 Section 5.1): 
o 
Antivirus software, including manual or managed updates of signatures or 
patterns; 
o 
Application whitelisting; or  
o 
Other method(s) to mitigate the introduction of malicious code. 
• 
For Transient Cyber Assets managed by a party other than LSPG (e.g. vendor) - Use 
one or a combination of the following prior to connecting the TCA to a low impact BES 
Cyber System per TCA capability (Att. 1 Section 5.2): 
o 
Review of antivirus update level; 
o 
Review of antivirus update process used by the party; 
o 
Review of application whitelisting used by the party; 
o 
Review use of live operating system and software executable only from read-only 
media; 
o 
Review of system hardening used by the party; or 
o 
Other method(s) to mitigate the introduction of malicious code. 
• 
LSPG shall determine whether any additional mitigation actions are necessary and 
implement such actions prior to connecting the Transient Cyber Asset (Att. 1 Section 
5.2.2). 
• 
For Removable Media – use each of the following (Att. 1 Section 5.3): 
o 
Method(s) to detect malicious code on Removable Media using a Cyber Asset 
other than a BES Cyber System (Att. 1 Section 5.3.1); and 
o 
Mitigation of the threat of detected malicious code on the Removable Media prior 
to connecting Removable Media to a low impact BES Cyber System (Att. 1 Section 
5.3.2).

units.section_text:
3.9 Declaring and responding to CIP Exceptional Circumstances 
Note: The processes for declaring a CIP Exceptional Circumstance covers high impact and 
medium impact BCS, and assets containing low impact BCS. 
3.9.1 
The CIP Senior Manager, or approved delegate, may declare an emergency as allowed per the 
CIP Exceptional Circumstance Procedure and may suspend any or all the following cyber 
security requirements: 
3.9.1.1 
Requirement to complete security training prior to authorization for unescorted physical 
access and/or authorization for electronic access to BES Cyber Systems (CIP-004 R2.2), 
3.9.1.2 
Requirement to authorize electronic or physical access based on need (CIP-004 R4.1), 
3.9.1.3 
Requirement for continuous visitor escort while within a Physical Security Perimeter (CIP-
006 R2.1), 
3.9.1.4 
Requirement for manual or automatic logging of visitor access to a Physical Security 
Perimeter (CIP-006 R2.2), 
3.9.1.5 
Requirement to retain applicable (security monitoring) event logs for at least the last 90 
consecutive calendar days (CIP-007 R4.3), and 
3.9.1.6 
Allow for Transient Cyber Assets and Removable Media that include the sections in 
Attachment 1 (CIP-010 R4, CIP-003 Att. 1 Sections 5.1 and 5.2). 
LSPG shall document the suspension of any of these cyber security policies including the reason and 
duration. Delegates are documented in a separate document maintained by the Reliability Compliance 
department.

units.requirement_text: The Responsible Entity shall implement a documented process to delegate authority, unless no delegations are used. Where allowed by the CIP Standards, the CIP Senior Manager may delegate authority for specific actions to a delegate or delegates. These delegations shall be documented, including the name or title of the delegate, the specific actions delegated, and the date of the delegation; approved by the CIP Senior Manager; and updated within 30 days of any change to the delegation. Delegation changes do not need to be reinstated with a change to the delegator.
units.section_text:
3.3 NERC CIP Activities Permitted for Delegation 
Pursuant to the NERC CIP Standards certain activities required of the NERC CIP Senior Manager may 
not be delegated. These are activities that the NERC CIP Standards have defined as obligations 
specifically required of the NERC CIP Senior Manager.  
Ownership and accountability for NERC CIP activities that are not CIP Senior Manager obligations are 
managed through other compliance procedures and do not need to be delegated in accordance with 
this Process.  
The following are NERC CIP Standards activities that have been approved by the COO and relevant 
senior leadership for delegation by the CIP Senior Manager:  
CIP Senior Manager Delegations 
3.3.1 
CIP-002-5.1a, R2.2: Approve the identifications of the high, medium, and low BES Cyber 
Systems required by Requirement R1 at least once every 15 calendar months, even if it has no 
identified items in Requirement R1. 
3.3.2 
CIP-003-8 (CIP-003-9, effective 4/1/26), R4: The Responsible Entity may delegate authority 
for specific actions under one or more cyber security policies to a delegate or delegates where 
allowed by the NERC CIP Standards. These delegations shall be documented in accordance 
with Section 3.2 and updated within 30 days of any change to the delegation.  
3.3.3 
CIP-007-6, R2.4: For each mitigation plan created or revised in R2.4, Part 2.3, implement the 
plan within the timeframe specified in the plan, unless a revision to the plan or an extension to 
the timeframe specified in Part 2.3 is approved by the CIP Senior Manager or delegate. 
3.3.4 
CIP-013-2, R3: Each Responsible Entity shall review and obtain CIP Senior Manager or delegate 
approval of its supply chain cyber security risk management plan(s) specified in Requirement 
R1 at least once every 15 calendar months. 
CIP Exceptional Circumstance Delegations 
3.3.5 
CIP-003-8 (CIP-003-9, effective 4/1/26), Attachment 1, Section 5: Each Responsible Entity 
shall, except under CIP Exceptional Circumstances, implement plans to achieve the objective 
of mitigating risk of the introduction of malicious code to low impact BES Cyber Systems 
through the use of Transient Cyber Assets and Removable Media. 

[LSP CIP Senior Manager Process] | Page 7 of 10 
Private – For Internal Use Only 
3.3.6 
CIP-004-7, R2.2: Require completion of the training specified in R2.2, Part 2.1 prior to granting 
authorized electronic access and authorized unescorted physical access to applicable Cyber 
Assets, except during CIP Exceptional Circumstances. 
3.3.7 
CIP-004-7, R4.1-R4.1.3: Process to authorize based on need, as determined by the 
Responsible Entity, except for CIP Exceptional Circumstances: electronic access; unescorted 
physical access into a Physical Security Perimeter; and access to designated storage locations, 
whether physical or electronic, for BES Cyber System Information. 
3.3.8 
CIP-006-6, R2.1 and R2.2: Require continuous escorted access of visitors (individuals who are 
provided access but are not authorized for unescorted physical access) within each Physical 
Security Perimeter, except during CIP Exceptional Circumstances. Require manual or 
automated logging of visitor entry into and exit from the Physical Security Perimeter that 
includes date and time of the initial entry and last exit, the visitor’s name, and the name of an 
individual point of contact responsible for the visitor, except during CIP Exceptional 
Circumstances. 
3.3.9 
CIP-007-6, R4.3: Where technically feasible, retain applicable event logs identified in R4.3, Part 
4.1 for at least the last 90 consecutive calendar days except under CIP Exceptional 
Circumstances. 
3.3.10 CIP-010-4, R3.3: Prior to adding a new applicable Cyber Asset to a production environment, 
perform an active vulnerability assessment of the new Cyber Asset, except for CIP Exceptional 
Circumstances and like replacements of the same type of Cyber Asset with a baseline 
configuration that models an existing baseline configuration of the previous or other existing 
Cyber Asset. 
3.3.11 
CIP-010-4, R4: Each Responsible Entity, for its high impact and medium impact BES Cyber 
Systems and associated Protected Cyber Assets, shall implement, except under CIP 
Exceptional Circumstances, one or more documented plan(s) for Transient Cyber Assets and 
Removable Media that include the sections in Attachment 1. 
3.3.12 
CIP-012-1 (CIP-012-2, effective 7/1/26), R1: The Responsible Entity shall implement, except 
under CIP Exceptional Circumstances, one or more documented plan(s) to mitigate the risks 
posed by unauthorized disclosure and unauthorized modification of Real-time Assessment and 
Real-time monitoring data while being transmitted between any applicable Control Centers.

3.1 
Quarterly and 15-month Review Overview 
3.1.1 
LSPG shall conduct reviews of individuals with active electronic access, unescorted 
physical access, and associated authorization records, including BCSI access, on a 
quarterly basis and at least once every 15 calendar months. 
3.1.2 
Quarterly and 15-calendar-month reviews require managers to validate that access 
privileges and authorizations remain appropriate for each of their direct reports. 
3.1.3 
OT Compliance will initiate and assign access reviews via email and track through the 
Change Management Solution. Reviewers will be provided access information only for 
personnel within their direct reporting structure. 
3.1.4 
The Compliance Tracking Tool automatically generates a task to complete the access 
review every 3-months and 15 calendar months.   
3.1.5 
After the evidence of the review has been uploaded to the Compliance Tracking Tool task, 
it is sent to the Manager, OT Security & Compliance for review and approval. 
Steps to Take  
3.2 
Electronic and Physical Access Review of Accounts, Privileges, and BCSI 
3.2.1 
This is the same process for both quarterly and 15-month reviews 
3.2.2 
The scope of this review is to verify that all individuals with provisioned access to the BES, 
associated EACMS, PACS and BCSI have an authorization record and still have a business 
need for access.  This includes employees, contractors, and vendors with access. 
3.2.2.1 
Scope includes but is not limited to:  
• 
High Impact BES Cyber Systems and their associated: 1. EACMS; and 2. PACS  
• 
Medium Impact BES Cyber Systems with External Routable Connectivity and 
their associated: 1. EACMS; and 2. PACS 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 6 of 8 
 
Steps to Take (to be performed for both electronic access and unescorted physical 
access authorizations): 
1) 
Review the standard to validate requirement and current version is correct. 
2) Create a staging folder for all evidence (folder label should include quarter/year 
identifier): L:\T_CTT\81.0 OT\CIP-004\Quarterly Access Reviews 
3) Compile system generated list of the following: 
1. 
Authorization records from change management solution 
2. Active users, accounts, and associated security groups including. 
• 
list of active personnel and vendors (domain and local accounts) 
• 
list of domain accounts (shared accounts) 
• 
list of local accounts (shared accounts) 
• 
list of active physical access accounts (PACS report) 
• 
PMP report (request from OT Compliance) 
3. BCSI repositories 
a. Request the following from OT security Operations. 
• 
S:\ Drive Operations Access Report  
• 
S:\ Drive Sysadmin Access Report 
• 
S:\ Drive Field Ops Access Report  
• 
OneDrive Access Report 
• 
ShareFile Access 
• 
Adept 
• 
Laserfiche Access Report 
• 
Armortext User Report 
• 
BigFix User Report 
• 
SFTP User Report 
b. Request the following from Field Operations: 
• 
PowerBase User Report 
c. Request the following from IT department: 
• 
T_CTT Folder Access Report 
d. Request the following from Transmission Compliance: 
• 
AssurX Access 
4. Verify all active users have authorization records and that that access was 
authorized prior to being granted. 
5. Map CIP users to managers as recorded in the Configuration Management 
Database (CMDB). 
6. Create user access sheets for each direct manager in CMDB. 
7. Email list of users, privileges, and current provisioning to direct managers for 
review and approval.  BCC changegear@lspower.com so the communication 
creates a ticket in the ticket management solution for tracking. 
8. After manager reviews are complete, stage all evidence for review.   
9. Create a summary report of findings and compile all lists into a master 
workbook. 
10. Open peer review ticket and assign it to OT Security and Compliance analyst. 
11. Once peer review is complete, attach completed workbook, source 
documents, and manager approvals/communication of validating existing 
privileges. 
12. Request approval.

3.1.5 
Access Revocation Program (R5) 
3.1.5.1 
LSPG shall document and implement an access revocation program to remove an individual’s 
access to BES Cyber Systems based upon the following conditions and timeframes: 
• 
For any termination action:  
o 
Revoke ability for unescorted physical access and Interactive Remote Access and 
complete the removals within 24 hours (Part 5.1);  
o 
Remove the individual’s ability to use provisioned access to BCSI by the end of the 
next calendar day following the effective date of the termination action (Part 6.3);  
o 
Revoke access to non-shared accounts within 30 days of the effective date of the 
termination action (Part 5.3, for High impact BES Cyber Systems and associated 
EACMS only); and/or 
o 
Change passwords to shared accounts known to the user within 30 calendar days 
of the termination action (Part 5.4, for High impact BES Cyber Systems and 
associated EACMS only)  
 
If LSPG determines there are extenuating operating circumstances which 
require a longer period of time for the password not to be changed, LSPG shall 
document such circumstances and change the shared account password 
within 10 calendar days following the end of the operating circumstance (Part 
5.4). 
 
 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 8 of 28 
 
• 
For reassignments or transfers:  
o 
Revoke authorized electronic access to individual accounts and authorized 
unescorted physical access no longer necessary by the end of the next calendar 
day following the date the access is no longer required (Part 5.2) and/or 
o 
Change passwords for shared accounts known to the user 30 days following the 
date access is no longer required (Part 5.4, for High impact BES Cyber Systems and 
associated EACMS only). 
 
If LSPG determines there are extenuating operating circumstances which 
require a longer period of time for the password not to be changed, LSPG shall 
document such circumstances and change the shared account password 
within 10 calendar days following the end of the operating circumstance (Part 
5.4).

units.section_text:
3.6 Access Revocation 
NOTE: All individual access will be disabled within 24 hours of notice of termination. This 
includes physical or electronic access. BCSI access will be revoked by the end of the next 
calendar day following the termination action. 
3.6.1 
Access revocation can be either planned or immediate. 
3.6.1.1 
Planned revocation is the scheduled revocation of unescorted physical and/or 
electronic access including BCSI. Planned revocation is when HR or the LSPG manager 
who oversees employees or contractors is aware of an employee or contractor 
termination\reassignment in advance of their last working day, e.g., retirement, voluntary 
separation of employment, transfer, end of project contract for vendors. 
3.6.1.1.1 
Notifications of planned revocations are sent to OT Security Operations and 
Transmission Reliability Compliance personnel via email from HR (for LSPG 
employees). The OT Administrators and/or OT Security Management ensure the 
AR is initiated. 
3.6.1.2 
Immediate revocation is the revocation of unescorted physical, electronic and/or BCSI 
access for those LSPG employees or contractors whose employment is ending 
immediately, e.g., termination or involuntary separation from company of either a LSPG 
employee or contractor from their company. 
3.6.1.2.1 
Notifications of immediate revocations can be sent by either HR or an LSPG 
Manager to either the OT Administrators or OT Security Management via phone 
call and/or email. The OT Administrators and/or OT Security Management ensure 
the AR is initiated. 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 9 of 17 
 
NOTE: All access accounts are disabled and not removed. This is done to show an audit 
trail of a user’s access and in the case where access may need to be reinstated (e.g., 
for personnel whose training has expired but will require access again once training is 
completed).

account(s) to expire at the end of business day listed as the termination, reassignment, 
or transfer date in the email notification. 
NOTE: Once the AD account(s) is disabled, the individual is unable to electronically 
access any other application or BCSI Repository they may have had access to, e.g., 
Interactive Remote Access.

units.section_text:
3.2.2 Access Methods 
3.2.2.1 
LSPG shall, where technically feasible, utilizes an Intermediate System such that the 
system outside an ESP may not initiate Interactive Remote Access (IRA) with a CIP Cyber 
Asset inside an ESP.  
3.2.2.2 
Intermediate Systems are maintained and monitored by OT Security Operations. 
3.2.2.3 
Restrictive firewall rules will be used and only ports and protocols required for accessing 
the Intermediate System servers will be allowed. 
3.2.2.4 
Where technically feasible, encryption shall be utilized between end user devices and 
Intermediate System servers, at a minimum, to protect against unauthorized interception 
of transmissions on communications links. 
3.2.2.5 
Remote access sessions are required to use an RDP client that utilizes encrypted 
communication channels. 
3.2.2.6 
IP ranges used by CIP Cyber Assets to communicate will be limited to known ranges of 
LSPG IP addresses on specific subnets or individual hosts. 
3.2.2.7 
Internal access to Intermediate Systems is limited to authorized users using specific 
LSPG IP ranges. 
3.2.2.8 
Where technically feasible, multi-factor authentication (MFA) will be used for all 
interactive Intermediate System server sessions, and privileges will be restricted to only 
what is required for authorized users. 
3.2.2.9 
External access to Intermediate Systems is limited to authorized users using only OT 
approved and maintained Multi-Factor Authentication methods, from specific LSPG IP 
ranges.

3.1 Vendor Remote Access Identification 
The term “Vendor” shall refer to those persons, companies, or other organizations with whom LSPG 
procures assets as well as related services. A Vendor may include: (i) developers or manufacturers of 
information systems, operational information systems, system components, or information and 
operational system services; (ii) product resellers; (iii) system integrators. A Vendor does not include 
other NERC Registered Entities providing reliability services (e.g., Reliability Coordinator services 
pursuant to NERC Reliability Standards).  
NERC CIP-005-7 R2, Part 2.4 requires one or more methods to determine active Vendor remote 
access session (i.e., including Interactive Remote Access and system-to-system remote access), and 
R3 Part 3.1 requires one or more methods to determine active Vendor initiated remote access session, 
which no Vendor is allowed to initiate (see section 3.1.2) and denied by LSPG’s security design. 
However, all Interactive Remote Access (IRA) sessions must follow OT Electronic Security Perimeters 
Procedure for remote access methods.  
For assets that contain low impact BCS, NERC CIP-003-9 R2 Attachment 1 Section 6.1 requires one or 
more method(s) for determining vendor electronic remote access for assets that contain low impact 
BCS.

units.section_text:
3.3.1 
Physical Security Plan (R1) 
3.3.1.1 
LSPG shall document and implement one or more physical security plans that: 
• 
Define operational or procedural controls to restrict physical access (Part 1.1), 
• 
Utilize at least one physical access control to allow unescorted physical access into 
each applicable Physical Security Perimeter to only those individuals who have 
authorized unescorted physical access (Part 1.2), 
• 
Where technically feasible, utilize two or more different physical access controls (this 
does not require two completely independent physical access control systems) to 
collectively allow unescorted physical access into Physical Security Perimeters to only 
those individuals who have authorized unescorted physical access (Part 1.3, for High 
impact BES Cyber Systems and associated EACMS and PCA only), 
• 
Monitor for unauthorized access through a physical access point into a Physical Security 
Perimeter (Part 1.4), 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 10 of 28 
 
• 
Issue an alarm or alert in response to detected unauthorized access through a physical 
access point into a Physical Security Perimeter to the personnel identified in the Cyber 
Security Incident response plan within 15 minutes of detection (Part 1.5), 
• 
Monitor each Physical Access Control System for unauthorized physical access to a 
Physical Access Control System (Part 1.6), 
• 
Issue an alarm or alert in response to detected unauthorized physical access to a 
Physical Access Control System to the personnel identified in the Cyber Security 
Incident response plan within 15 minutes of the detection (Part 1.7), 
• 
Log (through automated means or by personnel who control entry) entry of each 
individual with authorized unescorted physical access into each Physical Security 
Perimeter, with information to identify the individual and date and time of entry (Part 
1.8), 
• 
Retain physical access logs of entry of individuals with authorized unescorted physical 
access into each Physical Security Perimeter for at least 90 calendar days (Part 1.9), and 
• 
Restrict physical access to cabling and other nonprogrammable communication 
components used for connection between applicable Cyber Assets within the same 
Electronic Security Perimeter in those instances when such cabling and components are 
located outside of a Physical Security Perimeter (Part 1.10). 
o

units.section_text:
3.5 Protection of the PACS 
3.5.1 
LSPG protects and monitors for unauthorized physical access to the PACS by placing each 
local controller inside a locked cabinet in the PSP.  

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 9 of 18 
 
3.5.2 The primary ACM is located within a PSP at the TX Primary Control Center. The redundant 
ACM is located within the PSP at the TX Backup Control Center. 
3.5.3 The local controller inherits all the security measures implemented to protect the PSP. Each 
cabinet has a tamper switch as an additional physical security control. Each tamper switch 
has been configured to notify the Transmission System Operator (TSO) of any unauthorized 
access. 
3.5.4 The PACS is configured to monitor and log access 24x7 to the PSPs through its access 
control devices (e.g., card readers, PIN pads, door sensors, and local controllers). 
3.5.5 The PACS creates a log entry for, at a minimum: 
3.5.5.1 
Valid access card read 
3.5.5.2 Invalid access card read 
3.5.5.3 Door held open past threshold – 30 seconds 
3.5.5.4 Door forced 
3.5.5.5 Deactivated card attempt 
3.5.5.6 Tamper Notification 
3.5.6 In the event of PACS unavailability, loss of integrity of a PSP border, or other similar impacts 
on the physical security of a PSP, alternative measures shall be implemented for the duration 
of the event. These measures may include: 
3.5.6.1 
The use of physical keys to enter and/or exit a PSP in the event of a component or system 
failure. Refer to OT Key Management Work Instruction for guidance on obtaining a 
physical key. 
3.5.6.2 Video Surveillance – may only be used for investigative purposes only. 
3.5.6.3 Deploying an LSPG employee or contractor with authorized unescorted physical access 
to the PSP (within 15 minutes of notification of a system failure) to monitor the ACP until 
the PACS is restored. Logging of personnel into and out of the PSP during this time will 
be manually documented

3.2 Physical Security Perimeters (PSP) 
3.2.1 
LSPG has established PSPs to protect High Impact and Medium Impact BES Cyber Systems. 
3.2.2 Access Control Points (ACP) into PSPs have, at a minimum, the controls defined below to 
ensure physical security: 
3.2.2.1

3.2.2.3 
All ACPs are configured to alert in case of an unauthorized access attempt. Refer to 
Section 3.7 for more information on logging, monitoring, and alerting of physical access.

3.3.1 
Physical Security Plan (R1) 
3.3.1.1 
LSPG shall document and implement one or more physical security plans that: 
• 
Define operational or procedural controls to restrict physical access (Part 1.1), 
• 
Utilize at least one physical access control to allow unescorted physical access into 
each applicable Physical Security Perimeter to only those individuals who have 
authorized unescorted physical access (Part 1.2), 
• 
Where technically feasible, utilize two or more different physical access controls (this 
does not require two completely independent physical access control systems) to 
collectively allow unescorted physical access into Physical Security Perimeters to only 
those individuals who have authorized unescorted physical access (Part 1.3, for High 
impact BES Cyber Systems and associated EACMS and PCA only), 
• 
Monitor for unauthorized access through a physical access point into a Physical Security 
Perimeter (Part 1.4),

• 
Issue an alarm or alert in response to detected unauthorized access through a physical 
access point into a Physical Security Perimeter to the personnel identified in the Cyber 
Security Incident response plan within 15 minutes of detection (Part 1.5), 
• 
Monitor each Physical Access Control System for unauthorized physical access to a 
Physical Access Control System (Part 1.6), 
• 
Issue an alarm or alert in response to detected unauthorized physical access to a 
Physical Access Control System to the personnel identified in the Cyber Security 
Incident response plan within 15 minutes of the detection (Part 1.7), 
• 
Log (through automated means or by personnel who control entry) entry of each 
individual with authorized unescorted physical access into each Physical Security 
Perimeter, with information to identify the individual and date and time of entry (Part 
1.8), 
• 
Retain physical access logs of entry of individuals with authorized unescorted physical 
access into each Physical Security Perimeter for at least 90 calendar days (Part 1.9), and 
• 
Restrict physical access to cabling and other nonprogrammable communication 
components used for connection between applicable Cyber Assets within the same 
Electronic Security Perimeter in those instances when such cabling and components are 
located outside of a Physical Security Perimeter (Part 1.10). 
o

Encryption of data that transits such cabling and components; or

Monitoring the status of the communication link composed of such cabling 
and components and issuing an alarm or alert in response to detected 
communication failures to the personnel identified in the BES Cyber Security 
Incident response plan within 15 minutes of detection; or 
 
An equally effective logical protection.

but are not limited to:

partially/completely disabled) 
• 
Detected physical breach of an ACP 
• 
Detected electronic breach of an ACP

units.section_text:
3.5 Protection of the PACS 
3.5.1 
LSPG protects and monitors for unauthorized physical access to the PACS by placing each 
local controller inside a locked cabinet in the PSP.  

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 9 of 18 
 
3.5.2 The primary ACM is located within a PSP at the TX Primary Control Center. The redundant 
ACM is located within the PSP at the TX Backup Control Center. 
3.5.3 The local controller inherits all the security measures implemented to protect the PSP. Each 
cabinet has a tamper switch as an additional physical security control. Each tamper switch 
has been configured to notify the Transmission System Operator (TSO) of any unauthorized 
access. 
3.5.4 The PACS is configured to monitor and log access 24x7 to the PSPs through its access 
control devices (e.g., card readers, PIN pads, door sensors, and local controllers). 
3.5.5 The PACS creates a log entry for, at a minimum: 
3.5.5.1 
Valid access card read 
3.5.5.2 Invalid access card read 
3.5.5.3 Door held open past threshold – 30 seconds 
3.5.5.4 Door forced 
3.5.5.5 Deactivated card attempt 
3.5.5.6 Tamper Notification 
3.5.6 In the event of PACS unavailability, loss of integrity of a PSP border, or other similar impacts 
on the physical security of a PSP, alternative measures shall be implemented for the duration 
of the event. These measures may include: 
3.5.6.1 
The use of physical keys to enter and/or exit a PSP in the event of a component or system 
failure. Refer to OT Key Management Work Instruction for guidance on obtaining a 
physical key. 
3.5.6.2 Video Surveillance – may only be used for investigative purposes only. 
3.5.6.3 Deploying an LSPG employee or contractor with authorized unescorted physical access 
to the PSP (within 15 minutes of notification of a system failure) to monitor the ACP until 
the PACS is restored. Logging of personnel into and out of the PSP during this time will 
be manually documented

units.section_text:
3.5 Protection of the PACS 
3.5.1 
LSPG protects and monitors for unauthorized physical access to the PACS by placing each 
local controller inside a locked cabinet in the PSP.  

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 9 of 18 
 
3.5.2 The primary ACM is located within a PSP at the TX Primary Control Center. The redundant 
ACM is located within the PSP at the TX Backup Control Center. 
3.5.3 The local controller inherits all the security measures implemented to protect the PSP. Each 
cabinet has a tamper switch as an additional physical security control. Each tamper switch 
has been configured to notify the Transmission System Operator (TSO) of any unauthorized 
access. 
3.5.4 The PACS is configured to monitor and log access 24x7 to the PSPs through its access 
control devices (e.g., card readers, PIN pads, door sensors, and local controllers). 
3.5.5 The PACS creates a log entry for, at a minimum: 
3.5.5.1 
Valid access card read 
3.5.5.2 Invalid access card read 
3.5.5.3 Door held open past threshold – 30 seconds 
3.5.5.4 Door forced 
3.5.5.5 Deactivated card attempt 
3.5.5.6 Tamper Notification 
3.5.6 In the event of PACS unavailability, loss of integrity of a PSP border, or other similar impacts 
on the physical security of a PSP, alternative measures shall be implemented for the duration 
of the event. These measures may include: 
3.5.6.1 
The use of physical keys to enter and/or exit a PSP in the event of a component or system 
failure. Refer to OT Key Management Work Instruction for guidance on obtaining a 
physical key. 
3.5.6.2 Video Surveillance – may only be used for investigative purposes only. 
3.5.6.3 Deploying an LSPG employee or contractor with authorized unescorted physical access 
to the PSP (within 15 minutes of notification of a system failure) to monitor the ACP until 
the PACS is restored. Logging of personnel into and out of the PSP during this time will 
be manually documented

units.section_text:
3.4 Visitor Control during CECs  
3.4.1 
OT Visitor Control Program governs the LSPG visitor control process. 
3.4.2 There is no limit on the number of visitors for which an escort may be responsible during 
CECs. 
3.4.3 Escorts are NOT required to continuously monitor visitors inside the PSP or CIP-012 
Restricted Space during CECs. However, escorts shall make a reasonable effort to 
occasionally check on visitors required to be onsite during a CEC and ensure all activity in 
the PSP is appropriate.  
3.4.4 Escorts are NOT required to log all visitor ingress and egress.  
3.4.5 Emergency Event Coordinator or designated LSPG employee shall make best effort to 
collect and document names (first and last) and company, if available, of all affected 
personnel processed as exceptions during the CEC. 
3.4.6 The Physical Security Plan governs the LSPG physical security logging process. 
3.4.7 If the site PACS system, which performs primary logging functions, is not available, one or 
more of the following shall be used to document access to the site, but not limited to: 
3.4.7.1 
OT Control Center sites access logs 
3.4.7.2 
Corporate camera system 
3.4.7.3 
Local access logging as performed by issued security officers or other designated 
personnel 
3.4.7.4 
OT Security Operations logs at general office facilities or TSO logs for the substations. 
3.4.8 Monitoring for personnel not associated with the CEC shall be the responsibility of the 
Emergency Event Coordinator and/or any stationed security officers. 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 10 of 17 
 
3.4.9 LSPG employees are not required to be continuously stationed at the PSP access point(s) 
but shall be generally aware of the personnel located within the PSP and conduct frequent 
walk-downs to assess the site, safety permitting.

3.9 Declaring and responding to CIP Exceptional Circumstances 
Note: The processes for declaring a CIP Exceptional Circumstance covers high impact and 
medium impact BCS, and assets containing low impact BCS. 
3.9.1 
The CIP Senior Manager, or approved delegate, may declare an emergency as allowed per the 
CIP Exceptional Circumstance Procedure and may suspend any or all the following cyber 
security requirements: 
3.9.1.1 
Requirement to complete security training prior to authorization for unescorted physical 
access and/or authorization for electronic access to BES Cyber Systems (CIP-004 R2.2), 
3.9.1.2 
Requirement to authorize electronic or physical access based on need (CIP-004 R4.1), 
3.9.1.3 
Requirement for continuous visitor escort while within a Physical Security Perimeter (CIP-
006 R2.1), 
3.9.1.4 
Requirement for manual or automatic logging of visitor access to a Physical Security 
Perimeter (CIP-006 R2.2), 
3.9.1.5 
Requirement to retain applicable (security monitoring) event logs for at least the last 90 
consecutive calendar days (CIP-007 R4.3), and 
3.9.1.6 
Allow for Transient Cyber Assets and Removable Media that include the sections in 
Attachment 1 (CIP-010 R4, CIP-003 Att. 1 Sections 5.1 and 5.2). 
LSPG shall document the suspension of any of these cyber security policies including the reason and 
duration. Delegates are documented in a separate document maintained by the Reliability Compliance 
department.

units.requirement_text: Deploy method(s) to deter, detect, or prevent malicious code.
units.section_text:
3.1 Implementation  
3.1.1 
Before deployment of any CIP Cyber Asset(s), OT Security Operations will determine what 
Malware Software Prevention Tool (MSPT) will be appropriate and deploy that solution. 
3.1.2 
Deployment of the MSPT and its configuration shall be included in the CIP Cyber Asset 
configuration documentation within the Request for Change (RFC) as specified in the OT 
Change Management procedure. 
3.1.3 
For CIP Cyber Assets that are not capable of running MSPT (and/or third-party applications) 
are considered to have their own malware prevention by not allowing execution of third-party 
code. 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 7 of 9 
 
3.1.4 
When a compatible MSPT is not commercially available to put on a CIP Cyber Asset, utilize an 
integrated IDS to analyze inbound and outbound traffic to detect the propagation of malware 
and/or malicious traffic. 
3.1.5 
The Centralized Monitoring, Logging, and Alerting Platforms (CMLAP) monitors applicable CIP 
Cyber Assets by establishing event monitoring settings triggering alerts when behavior that may 
indicate infection is observed (e.g., unexplained file or directory creation, unusual CPU activity, 
etc.). 
3.1.5.1 
CMLAP is a suite of tools which may include, but is not limited to Tripwire, CMLAP, Armortext, 
Symantec, NPM, Nessus, and IP360.

units.section_text:
3.1.6 
Mitigate the Introduction of Malicious Code (Section 1.4) 
Prior to use on applicable systems, the OT Security Operations team utilizes Antivirus Software (AV) 
as the method to mitigate the introduction of malicious code in accordance with the OT Malicious 
Code Prevention Process. During the build process of a TCA, AV software is installed.  
TCA are required to be connected to the network on a defined date every month to receive security 
patch updates as described in Section 2.1.5 above. During the connection to the network, TCA will 
receive AV software and pattern file updates to the current version(s). TCA connected to the network 
since the most recent monthly update and before the next scheduled monthly update may receive 
additional AV updates. Prior to connecting to applicable systems, TCA must have updated AV 
signature files at a minimum of monthly during patching cycles. Documentation of monthly AV 
software and pattern file updates is tracked through the OT Change Management Procedure. 
In the event a TCA does not receive the monthly AV update, the TCA is pulled from service and 
required to be updated to the most current version(s) prior to connecting to any applicable systems.  
If a TCA is identified as having malicious code, OT Security Operations follows the OT Security 
Incident Response Plan.

3.3.4 Mitigate the Introduction of Malicious Code (Section 3.2, 3.2.1) 
LSPG uses RM to perform maintenance on applicable systems. As a protective measure, OT Security 
Operations logically disables ports not in use. Prior to being plugged into a BES Cyber System or PCA, 
the user plugs the RM into a TCA which has current signature files per Section 2.1.6 and scans the RM 
for possible malicious code. If malicious code is found during the scan of the RM, the TCA should be 
quarantined and rescanned prior to being connected to the BCS or PCA. Evidence of using RM and the 
scan is maintained in the change management solution repository, per the OT Change Management 
Procedure. 
If the RM is identified as having malicious code prior to connecting to an applicable system, LSPG 
follows the OT Security Incident Response Plan.

units.section_text:
3.4.4 Security Event Monitoring Process (R4) 
3.4.4.1 
LSPG shall document and implement a security event monitoring process to: 
• 
Log events at the BES Cyber System level (per BES Cyber System capability) or at the 
Cyber Asset level (per Cyber Asset capability) for identification of, and after-the-fact 
investigations of, Cyber Security Incidents that includes, as a minimum, each of the 
following types of events (Part 4.1): 
o 
Detected successful login attempts (Part 4.1.1), 
o 
Detected failed access attempts and failed login attempts (Part 4.1.2), and 
o 
Detected malicious code (Part 4.1.3). 
• 
Configure the monitoring system to generate alerts for security events that LSPG 
determines necessitates an alert, that includes, as a minimum, each of the following 
types of events (per Cyber Asset or BES Cyber System capability) (Part 4.2): 
o 
Detected malicious code (Part 4.2.1), and 
o 
Detected failure of event logging (Part 4.2.2). 
• 
LSPG shall retain applicable event logs for at least the last 90 consecutive calendar days 
except under CIP Exceptional Circumstances, where technically feasible (Part 4.3), and 
• 
LSPG shall review a summarization or sampling of logged events as determined by LSPG 
at intervals no greater than 15 calendar days to identify undetected Cyber Security 
Incidents (Part 4.4).

3.1.3 
Shared Accounts 
3.1.3.1 
A shared account is an account with credentials (login name and password) known to 
multiple, authorized users. Shared accounts may include: 
• 
Administrator/root accounts,  
• 
Factory/default accounts,  
• 
Accounts required for scheduled and automated tasks, and  
• 
Generic accounts that are required by the installed applications/databases. 
3.1.3.2 
Access to shared accounts is based on roles, which is based on an individual’s job 
function and their need to know. 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 7 of 16 
 
• 
Access to existing shared accounts is authorized through the submission of an AR 
by following the OT Access Management Procedure. 
• 
Access/creation of a new shared account is authorized through the submission of 
a Request for Change (RFC) by following the OT Change Management Procedure. 
3.1.3.3 
Shared accounts for devices are recorded in the EPM system.  
3.1.3.4 
Where possible, a user must log into any CIP Cyber Asset with their assigned individual 
account credentials and access the EPM system to retrieve a shared account password. 
3.1.3.5 
Shared accounts are used only when necessary and removed where possible. Access to 
these accounts must be kept to a minimum. Users shall only use the shared accounts 
when their role or responsibility requires them to.

3.4.5 System Access Controls Process (R5) 
3.4.5.1 
LSPG shall document and implement a system access control process to: 
• 
Define a method(s) to enforce authentication of interactive user access, where 
technically feasible (Part 5.1), 
• 
Identify and inventory all known enabled default or other generic account types, either 
by system, by groups of systems, by location, or by system type(s) (Part 5.2), 
• 
Identify individuals who have authorized access to shared accounts (Part 5.3), 
• 
Change known default passwords, per Cyber Asset capability (Part 5.4), and 
• 
For password-only authentication for interactive user access, either technically or 
procedurally, enforce the following password parameters (Part 5.5): 
o 
Password length that is, at least, the lesser of eight characters or the maximum 
length supported by the Cyber Asset (Part 5.5.1), and 
o 
Minimum password complexity that is the lesser of three or more different types 
of characters (e.g., uppercase alphabetic, lowercase alphabetic, numeric, non- 
alphanumeric) or the maximum complexity supported by the Cyber Asset (Part 
5.5.2). 
• 
For password-only authentication for interactive user access, where technically 
feasible, either technically or procedurally enforce password changes or an obligation 
to change the password at least once every 15 calendar months (Part 5.6), and 
• 
LSPG shall, where technically feasible, either: 
o 
Limit the number of unsuccessful authentication attempts, or 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 13 of 28 
 
o 
Generate alerts after a threshold of unsuccessful authentication attempts (Part 
5.7).

units.section_text:
5.5.1 
Criteria to Evaluate and Define Attempts to Compromise 
5.5.1.1 
LSPG defines an attempt to compromise as a malicious effort to gain access to a BES 
Cyber System that is not authorized and does not infiltrate the BES Cyber System. 
Malicious effort is determined by: 
5.5.1.1.1 
Multiple unsuccessful attempts into multiple Cyber Assets which meet or exceed 
the thresholds put in place by LSPG, Section 5.4  
5.5.1.1.2 
LSPG cannot confirm contact with the person (or their manager) in question 
attempting access, or 
5.5.1.1.3 
The attempted access is coming from an outside source.

3.5.2 Cyber Security Incident Response Plan Implementation and Testing Process (R2) 
3.5.2.1 
For high impact and medium impact BCS, and their associated EACMS, LSPG shall document 
and implement a Cyber Security Incident response plan to collectively include each of the 
applicable requirement parts in CIP-008-6 Table R2 – Cyber Security Incident Response Plan 
Implementation and Testing: 
• 
Test each Cyber Security Incident response plan(s) at least once every 15 calendar 
months using one of the following scenarios: 
o 
By responding to an actual Reportable Cyber Security Incident, 
o 
With a paper drill or tabletop exercise of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident, or 
o 
With an operational exercise of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident (Part 2.1). 
• 
Use the Cyber Security Incident response plan(s) when responding to a Reportable 
Cyber Security Incident or performing an exercise of a Reportable Cyber Security 
Incident. LSPG shall document deviations from the plan(s) taken during the response 
to the incident or exercise (Part 2.2), and 
• 
Retain records related to Reportable Cyber Security Incidents (Part 2.3). 
3.5.2.2 
For assets containing low impact BCS, LSPG shall test the Cyber Security Incident response 
plan(s) at least once every 36 calendar months by: 
o 
Responding to an actual Reportable Cyber Security Incident,

6.1.7 
Reporting Timeframes (Applicable to CIP) 
6.1.7.1 
If the incident was determined to be a Reportable Cyber Security Incident by the SIRT 
Team and the Director, Operations Technology, the SIRT Lead has one (1) hour to 
complete the OE-417 form Reliability First and/or other methods to notify E-ISAC and 
NCCIC.  
• 
The name of individual(s), date and time when the determination was made, and 
date and time the form was submitted are captured on the Security Incident 
Investigation Form. 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 23 of 46 
 
6.1.7.2 
If the incident was determined to be an attempt to compromise a system, the SIRT Lead 
has until the end of the next calendar day to complete and submits the appropriate 
form(s) to E-ISAC and NCCIC.  
• 
The name of individual(s), date and time when the determination was made, and 
date and time the form was submitted are captured on the Security Incident 
Investigation Form. 
6.1.7.3 
The SIRT Lead provides updates to E-ISAC and NCCIC within 7 calendar days of 
determination of any new or changed information from the initial notification.  
• 
The name of individual(s), date, time, and when the updates were made are 
documented on the Security Incident Investigation Form.

units.section_text:
3.2 Recovery Plan Activation 
3.2.1 
This procedure shall be enacted at the discretion of OT, EMS, or Field Ops Management 
under conditions that may pose a risk to the reliability of the Bulk Electric System. Conditions 
shall include, but not be limited to, the following:  
3.2.1.1 
If the configuration or settings of a Cyber Asset or a series of Cyber Assets fails or 
become unusable 
3.2.1.2 
If a Cyber Asset or a series of Cyber Asset hardware fails or becomes unusable 
Note: The Recovery Plan may not necessarily be executed in its entirety for break/fix priority events, 
though certain components (i.e. restoration steps) may be used to assist in problem resolution.

LSPG utilizes both automated and manual processes to backup applicable CIP Cyber Assets.

3.6 Backup Procedure 
3.6.1 
LSPG utilizes both automated and manual processes to backup applicable CIP Cyber Assets.  
3.6.1.1 
For systems and devices backed up via automated backup tools, in a server/client 
arrangement, LSPG will utilize the option within the backup software to verify and 
validate a backup upon successful completion of the backup.  
3.6.1.2 
All devices that cannot, or due to operational reasons, will not be backed up by an 
automated backup tool, shall be backed up on an “as needed” basis by the device 
owner. 
3.6.2 The table below describes one (1) or more processes that LSPG utilizes for the backup and 
storage of information required to recover BCS functionality.

that do not fall within these common categories, or cannot be backed up because of

units.section_text:
3.6.3 For High Impact BCS and their associated EACMS and PACS, successful completion of the 
backup processes described in the table above shall be made, verified by reports that are 
automatically generated and maintained by OT Security Operations and/or OT Security & 
Compliance.  
3.6.4 These reports show any device or configuration backups that have failed. 
3.6.4.1 
Manually process device backup and run report to validate successful completion. 
3.6.4.2 For any device or configuration backups that have failed and do not successfully 
backup manually, refer to the applicable work instruction identified in the above table 
to validate backup configuration and/or perform device recovery. 
3.6.5 Automated backups of devices shall be completed based on the system requirements. A 
daily incremental or differential backup with a full weekly backup shall be completed for 
systems with high rates of change, when possible. Other devices with manual backup 
procedures shall be backed up after changes/upgrades to the device are implemented.

units.section_text:
3.7 Data Preservation Procedures 
3.7.1 
Data, per Cyber Asset capability, shall be preserved for determining the cause of a real or 
potential Cyber Security Incident that triggers the activation of the Recovery Plan. Data 
preservation shall not impede or restrict recovery.  
3.7.2 Any data determined to be related to an actual Cyber Security Incident shall be preserved 
according to the Cyber Security Incident Response Plan. 
3.7.3 Physical data storage media and/or images shall be destroyed on or after the appropriate 
date in accordance with OT BES Cyber Asset Reuse & Disposal.

3.1 Recovery Plan 
3.1.1 
LSPG has developed and implemented a series of processes, procedures and work 
instructions to restore in-scope systems from unpredicted cyber or physical event(s) that 
impact the reliability and operation of all OT managed systems. The Recovery Plan describes 
the process to assess the conditions for the activation of the Recovery Plan, the roles and 
responsibilities of responders, and the backup and storage process to recover BES Cyber 
System functionality.

units.section_text:
3.8 Recovery Plan Testing  
3.8.1 
OT, EMS, and Field Ops shall test the Recovery Plans for High and Medium Impact BCS and 
their associated EACMS and PACS at control centers at least once every fifteen (15) calendar 
months. 
Note: LSPG does not have any Medium Impact Control Centers. 
3.8.2  The test shall be one of the following methods.  
3.8.2.1 
Recovery from an actual incident; 
3.8.2.2 
With a paper drill or tabletop exercise; or, 
3.8.2.3 
With an operational exercise. 
3.8.3 OT, EMS, and Field Ops shall test the Recovery Plans for High Impact BCS at least once every 
36 calendar months through an operational exercise. 
3.8.3.1 
The test environment shall be representative of the production environment. 
3.8.3.2 
An actual recovery response may substitute for an operational exercise. 
3.8.4 OT, EMS, and Field Ops shall initiate a request for all testing performed.  
Note: For operational exercise scenarios, LSPG may use reasonable alternatives to recovery actions 
that may otherwise incur additional costs, e.g. the use of spare, test, or dev equipment in lieu of 
ordering replacement hardware from vendors. In all such cases, these alternative actions will be 
validated and documented, such that minimal differentiation from actual recovery actions can be 
maintained.

units.section_text:
3.0 Process 
The automated work instruction is defined to run monthly, as to not impact the daily discovery scan 
the profilers perform weekdays. 
3.1 
Enable Only Necessary Logical Network Accessible Ports CIP-007-6 R1.1 
3.1.1 
The port justification table is listed in the OT Firewall Management Work Instructions  for 
establishing consistency in port justifications. Before promoting new ports and services, use 
the approved justifications listed in OT Firewall Management Work Instructions . 
3.1.2 
The VAT Scanner Ports and Services scan is set up to be recurring per 3.1.3, on the in-scope 
networks at high and medium locations. 
3.1.3 
The “Profile” name must remain the same as this is the only scan that is exported from the 
VAT Scanner using the automated mechanism to allow Change Monitoring Solution server to 
locate the results and import them as defined below: 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 6 of 16 
 
 
3.1.4 
The schedule is typically configured as shown below: 
 
 
3.1.5 
Once the VAT Scanner Ports and Services scan has completed and results show in activity 
as complete, the integration process is scheduled to run weekly to gather the results and 
import to Change Monitoring Solution. 
3.1.6 
If network devices or appliances (agentless) are added to the VAT Scanner between the 
weekly automated process, end users should go into the Change Monitoring Solution 
console to the “Tasks” tab, expand the Root Task Group folder, then select Tripwire State 
Analyzer tasks. 
3.1.7 
The TSA process must be executed in the following order: 
3.1.7.1 
Agentless – AD HOC Run IP360cmd create nmap rule. Wait for it to complete, then 
proceed to step 2. 
3.1.7.2 
Agentless – TSA - 2 – WLP – Weekly – Process External Data. Wait for it to complete. 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 7 of 16 
 
 
3.1.8 
After the data is processed, the associated output files are automatically created on the 
Change Monitoring Solution server. 
3.1.9 
Only users with administrative privileges and management approval are able to access and 
update the whitelist on the server. 
3.1.10 
Justifications for ports and services, including vendor documentation or SME attestation, 
must be available to update the whitelist. 
3.1.11 
Enable host-based firewall rules for any ports and services that cannot be removed or 
deleted on devices that have a host-based firewall. 
3.1.12 
This process also updates the ports and services component of the baseline for the asset. 
3.2 
Configuration Change Monitoring At Least Once Every 35 Days CIP-010-4 R2.1 
3.2.1 
OT Security Operations / OT Security & Compliance team or delegate will perform a periodic 
review, as close to daily as possible, of the OT Last Time Checked Status Report that details 
the communication status of assets reporting to Change Monitoring Solution. 
3.2.2 
A Change Management Solution ticket will be created system with the short description 
“Remediation of OT Last Time Checked Status Report.” 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 8 of 16 
 
 
3.2.3 
Once created, confirm that Assigned Tech is the primary SME. 
3.2.4 
Any new nodes on the report will be triaged to confirm they are not related to work being 
performed under an active RFC or incident ticket. 
3.2.4.1 
TCAs are excluded from the scope of this task. 
3.2.5 
The team will investigate nodes to determine if the event is a one-time anomaly or requires 
further investigation. Best efforts will be made to perform the investigation on the same day 
and not to exceed five business days. 
3.2.6 
In-scope CIP Cyber Assets should be prioritized for remediation. 
3.2.7 
Classifications can be validated by going to Asset View, search by host name or IP address, 
and reviewing node Tag Sets as shown in the screenshot below: 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 9 of 16 
 
 
 
3.2.8 
If the Classification is not defined in Change Monitoring Solution, go to OTAM CMDB to 
retrieve the Classification. (Note – If device is not in OTAM CMDB, investigation needs to 
occur via creation of a Change Management Solution ticket) 
• 
Classifications can be updated by: 
• 
Select the check mark before the host name, 
• 
Click Edit Tags in the right menu bar, 
• 
Click the Classification menu and select correct option, 
• 
Click close. 
 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 10 of 16 
 
 
3.2.9 
If event is determined to not be an anomaly and requires further troubleshooting, OT Security 
Operations / OT Security & Compliance team will remediate. 
3.2.10 Remediation includes: 
3.2.10.1 
Document the open RFC impacting connectivity (if applicable). 
3.2.10.2 Log into the asset and restart the Change Monitoring Solution agent (servers and 
workstations). 
3.2.10.3 Reinstall Configuration Change Monitoring Solution agent. 
3.2.10.4 For agentless assets (network devices/appliances), contact the assigned SME about 
configuration change that is impacting communication with Change Monitoring Solution 
console. 
3.2.11 
If the assigned SME is not available, forward the ticket to the SME on call. 
3.2.12 
Once the assigned SME performs remediation, the ticket should be routed back to the 
Primary SME for validation that asset is reporting back to Change Monitoring Solution. 
Once configuration change monitoring is validated as reporting to the solution, the Primary 
SME should document resolution notes in the ticket and close it. 
3.3 
Develop, Authorizing and Document Changes That Deviate from Existing Baseline 
Configuration CIP-010-4 R1.1, R1.2 and R1.3 
3.3.1 
Change promotions in Change Monitoring Solution require research and validation against 
the changes described in the official RFC. 
3.3.2 
Change Monitoring Solution detects deviations from the baseline. OT Security Operations/ 
OT Security & Compliance is required to validate that changes are authorized before 
promoting (approving) the new baseline.  
Separation of duties 
a. Detection of unauthorized changes alert configured (Daily Tripwire Report is

3.7.4.1 
For high impact and medium impact BCS, LSPG shall implement, except during CIP

Removable Media: 
• 
Transient Cyber Assets

o

o

•

o 
Malicious Code Mitigation 
3.7.4.2 
For assets containing low impact BCS, LSPG shall implement, except during CIP Exceptional 
Circumstances, one or more documented plan(s) to mitigate the risk of the introduction of 
malicious code to low impact BCS through the use of Transient Cyber Assets (TCA) and 
Removable Media (RM). The plan(s) shall include: 
• 
For Transient Cyber Assets managed by LSPG – use one or a combination of the 
following in an ongoing or on-demand manner per TCA capability (Att. 1 Section 5.1): 
o 
Antivirus software, including manual or managed updates of signatures or 
patterns; 
o 
Application whitelisting; or  
o 
Other method(s) to mitigate the introduction of malicious code. 
• 
For Transient Cyber Assets managed by a party other than LSPG (e.g. vendor) - Use 
one or a combination of the following prior to connecting the TCA to a low impact BES 
Cyber System per TCA capability (Att. 1 Section 5.2): 
o 
Review of antivirus update level; 
o 
Review of antivirus update process used by the party; 
o 
Review of application whitelisting used by the party; 
o 
Review use of live operating system and software executable only from read-only 
media; 
o 
Review of system hardening used by the party; or 
o 
Other method(s) to mitigate the introduction of malicious code. 
• 
LSPG shall determine whether any additional mitigation actions are necessary and 
implement such actions prior to connecting the Transient Cyber Asset (Att. 1 Section 
5.2.2). 
• 
For Removable Media – use each of the following (Att. 1 Section 5.3): 
o 
Method(s) to detect malicious code on Removable Media using a Cyber Asset 
other than a BES Cyber System (Att. 1 Section 5.3.1); and 
o 
Mitigation of the threat of detected malicious code on the Removable Media prior 
to connecting Removable Media to a low impact BES Cyber System (Att. 1 Section 
5.3.2).

3.2 Protection and Handling Guidelines (Part 1.2) 
All LSPG Personnel, contractors, and vendors, hereinafter referred to as LSPG users, are responsible 
for protecting and maintaining the confidentiality of all BCSI. All LSPG users shall report violations of 
this policy to the Sr. Director, Operations Technology or the Reliability Compliance Team. Any LSPG
